newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai hotel fire search continues, toll hits 90.
newsitem.headline: Thai hotel fire search continues, toll hits 90.

text.p: Thai police and rescue workers on Sunday combed the devastated third floor of a 16-storey beachfront hotel for bodies, two days after a fire which killed at least 90.
Charred remains of seven people were discovered on Saturday on the third floor of Pattaya's 400-room Royal Jomtien Resort Hotel before the search was called off for the night.
"The third level had many function rooms and lobbies where people gathered. It is possible we shall find some more people there," said one rescue team supervisor.

He said searchers planned to focus their efforts on a large function room with a caved-in roof. Several hundred people had been attending seminars on the third floor on Friday and were trapped after the fire broke out.
The 90 known dead in Thailand's worst hotel fire tragedy included at least 10 foreigners and about 30 hotel staff. Apart from the dead, almost 70 people were injured, some critically.

Disaster relief officials said eight rescue workers racing from Bangkok to Pattaya, about 200 km (125 miles) southeast of the capital, were also killed on Friday after their pick-up truck was in collision with another vehicle.
Police said the fire was started by a cooking gas explosion in the hotel's ground-floor cafeteria and spread rapidly, fanned by a strong sea breeze.
Police said the high death toll was partly due to locked fire exits on the first few storeys of the hotel. Most victims died from suffocation while many were burned beyond recognition.
Police said the management of the Royal Jomtien hotel may have locked emergency doors to prevent theft or stop hotel guests from leaving without paying bills.
Many guests told reporters the hotel's sprinklers and smoke alarm system did not work.
Speaking on Saturday, Interior Minister Snoh Thienthong blamed the disaster on the hotel's decision to store cooking gas tanks in its indoor kitchens.
He said government agencies would hold urgent meetings on Monday to boost safety facilities at high buildings and public places.

An official of the Tourist Authority of Thailand said a group of more than 40 Korean tourists had had a lucky escape on Friday morning, leaving the Royal Jomtien for a tour of an island off Pattaya shortly before the fire broke out.
But he said the group's tour leader had stayed behind at the hotel to rest and she was among three Koreans to die.
Other foreigners killed in the fire included six Hungarians and a Belgian.
